reason: A testa whose cells or thickenings lie in long parallel transverse bars like the rungs of a ladder. FLOPO scalariform defines this; 'linear' only says the bars are long and narrow.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: green PATO_0000320 – dark green PATO_0001249)
reason: A range between two existing colour values ('mid green' is plain green). The continuum relation handles it, as with oblong-ovate.

Chalky leaves (Dudleya and others) are covered with a white, powdery waxy bloom, the same reading as pruinose (rule C222). In 'pale chalky pink' the word only modifies a colour, and the colour (pink PATO_0000954) carries the value.

label: corm-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a corm: a short, erect, swollen, solid stem base. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991325 rhizome-like and FLOPO:0991359 stolon-like; not FLOPO:0991109 tuberous, which is irregularly swollen.
reason: Used of the caudex or stem base of Isoetes-like and geophytic plants ('caudex cormoid', 'not cormoid'). It follows the precedent of rhizome-like; the part is corm PO_0025355 only by resemblance.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: pinnately lobed FLOPO:0991157 – palmately lobed FLOPO:0991158), with the '1(–2)-' prefix as the order of division in docs/odp/05-range-with-extremes.md
reason: A lobing between pinnate and palmate, preceded by how many times the blade is lobed. Both values exist, so no new term is needed.

Same reading as 'ray-like' (second-model review 2026-11-14): a corolla or floret that looks like the ligule of a ray flower (PO_0025331). It does not capture the enlarged funnel-shaped sterile florets of Centaurea.

target: new: indumentum with its hair type (pannose PATO_0104242 on the organ + star shaped PATO_0002065 on its hairs, trichome PO_0000282)
reason: Two values with different bearers: the organ is felted and its hairs are stellate. Treated as stellate-velutinous was (2026-11-14).

target: new: part of the bearer (barb trichome, trichome PO_0000282) + antrorse (PATO_0002238)
reason: FLOPO barbed (FLOPO:0991209) and barbellate (FLOPO:0991087) are defined by barbs that point backwards, so 'antrorsely barbed' contradicts both. The quality is the forward direction of the barbs on the awn, bristle or fruit margin.
A key-couplet phrase about the hypanthium cup (PO_0009065) that negates a part (the rim, which has no class) and two of its qualities at once. It cannot be grounded safely as an absence.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (loose PATO_0001802 towards achene fruit PO_0030107)
reason: The perigynium's relation to the achene inside it. A relation with its second term, not a quality of the perigynium alone.
As with 'purple-tinged' (2026-11-14), the colour is the value and 'suffused' only weakens it. It may take an 'approximately' qualifier.

A quality of the inflorescence towards its flowers: the flowers are closely packed. Like 'few-flowered' it is stated of the whole through its parts; it is a density, not a count, so it does not belong under pattern 13.
'Obscurely' weakens the existing value trigonous in the same way as 'sub-' does, which pattern 01 covers.
A compound of two existing shape values, handled by the continuum relation as with oblong-ovate.

target: docs/odp/10-ratio-to-another-part.md (equality of colour towards sepal PO_0009031)
reason: An equality to another part that names its second term. Pattern 10 covers equalities ('as long as'); colour is a new attribute for it.

Vernicose means glossy as if varnished; PATO glistening has the exact synonyms glossy and shiny, the same target as 'lustrous'. Where floras mean a sticky varnish, it is closer to glutinous PATO_0001540.
Phacellaria is parasitic on other mistletoes; the plant is parasitic, and that its host is itself a parasite is a relation to another taxon, which the patterns do not model.
Pruinose maps to glaucous (rule C222). This is its negation, in the same form as unlobed.

target: new: two values of one bearer (oblong PATO_0000946 and falciform PATO_0002215)
reason: Not a continuum: the outline is oblong and curved like a sickle, so both values hold together, as with obliquely ovate.

target: dimorphic (FLOPO:0991092) of the flowers of the inflorescence
reason: An inflorescence bearing flowers of two kinds; FLOPO dimorphic inheres in the set of flowers. When the kinds are sexual, heterogamous (FLOPO:0991178) is the better target.
Lens-shaped = lenticular, which rule C202 maps to biconvex. The gland example is a transcription fragment.
Capillary pappus bristles are hair-like and very fine; 'hair-like' maps to filiform (rule C317).
A compound of two existing shape values, handled by the continuum relation.

label: scobiform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a seed by virtue of its being minute, thin and elongate, so that the seeds of a fruit together resemble sawdust. NOTE: Botany-specific (Orchidaceae, Ericaceae, Orobanchaceae).
reason: A recognised botanical term (scobiform) for dust-like seeds. No PATO or FLOPO size or shape value says it, and it is a quality of the seed, not a part.

target: docs/odp/16-quality-of-a-whole-towards-its-parts.md (parallel to PATO_0002272 among the locules or veins) with docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md
reason: PATO 'parallel to' is relational: the locules or veins are parallel to one another. 'Nearly' is the approximate qualifier.
Same meaning as FLOPO evenly spaced (synonyms regularly spaced, equidistant); the Spanish 'uniformemente espaciadas' too.

target: new: presence of a cell inclusion (raphide; no PO or FLOPO class, needs a FLOPO anatomy class) on the part, docs/odp/15-absence-of-a-part.md form
reason: A presence statement (a Rubiaceae key character), but raphides, needle-like calcium oxalate crystals in cells, have no PO class. It cannot be an entity-presence rule until a bearer class exists.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: triangular PATO_0001875 – ovate PATO_0001891, synonym ovoid)
reason: A compound of two existing shape values, handled by the continuum relation.

target: docs/odp/15-absence-of-a-part.md (absence of nectary PO_0009035 qualified by concave PATO_0001857)
reason: Only concave nectaries are denied, not nectaries as such, so a plain absence rule for nectary would overstate it. It needs the absence of a qualified part.
Moss leaf cells that are rectangular and only somewhat longer than wide. 'Short' and 'irregularly' are degree modifiers that are not kept, as with 'broadly acute'.
